passages.text: These are the proverbs of Solomon son of David, king of Israel, for gaining wisdom and discipline, for comprehending words of insight, and for receiving instruction in wise living and in righteousness, justice, and equity.
passages.sermon:
Solomon was the son of David.
Solomon was the king of Israel.
These are Solomon’s proverbs.
These proverbs help people gain wisdom.
These proverbs teach discipline.
These proverbs help people understand words of insight.
These proverbs give instruction for wise living.
These proverbs teach righteousness.
These proverbs teach justice.
These proverbs teach equity.
passages.original: מִ֭שְׁלֵי שְׁלֹמֹ֣ה בֶן־ דָּוִ֑ד מֶ֝֗לֶךְ יִשְׂרָאֵֽל׃ לָדַ֣עַת חָכְמָ֣ה וּמוּסָ֑ר לְ֝הָבִ֗ין אִמְרֵ֥י בִינָֽה׃ לָ֭קַחַת מוּסַ֣ר הַשְׂכֵּ֑ל צֶ֥דֶק וּ֝מִשְׁפָּ֗ט וּמֵישָׁרִֽים׃

passages.text: To impart prudence to the simple and knowledge and discretion to the young, let the wise listen and gain instruction, and the discerning acquire wise counsel by understanding the proverbs and parables, the sayings and riddles of the wise.
passages.sermon:
These proverbs give prudence to simple people.
They give knowledge to young people.
They give discretion to young people.
Wise people listen to these proverbs.
Wise people gain more instruction.
Discerning people acquire wise counsel.
They do this by understanding proverbs.
They do this by understanding parables.
They understand the sayings of wise people.
They understand the riddles of wise people.
passages.original: לָתֵ֣ת לִפְתָאיִ֣ם עָרְמָ֑ה לְ֝נַ֗עַר דַּ֣עַת וּמְזִמָּֽה׃ יִשְׁמַ֣ע חָ֭כָם וְי֣וֹסֶף לֶ֑קַח וְ֝נָב֗וֹן תַּחְבֻּל֥וֹת יִקְנֶֽה׃ לְהָבִ֣ין מָ֭שָׁל וּמְלִיצָ֑ה דִּבְרֵ֥י חֲ֝כָמִ֗ים וְחִידֹתָֽם׃

passages.text: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge, but fools despise wisdom and discipline.
passages.sermon: The fear of the LORD is the beginning of knowledge.\r\nFools despise wisdom.\r\nFools despise discipline.
passages.original: יִרְאַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה רֵאשִׁ֣ית דָּ֑עַת חָכְמָ֥ה וּ֝מוּסָ֗ר אֱוִילִ֥ים בָּֽזוּ׃פ

passages.text: Listen, my son, to your father’s instruction, and do not forsake the teaching of your mother.
passages.sermon:
A father gives instruction to his son.
A mother teaches her son.
My son, listen to your father’s instruction.
Do not abandon your mother’s teaching.
passages.original: שְׁמַ֣ע בְּ֭נִי מוּסַ֣ר אָבִ֑יךָ וְאַל־ תִּ֝טֹּ֗שׁ תּוֹרַ֥ת אִמֶּֽךָ׃

passages.text: For they are a garland of grace on your head and a pendant around your neck.
passages.sermon:
A father’s instruction and a mother’s teaching are very valuable.
They bring honor and beauty to your life.
They are like a graceful garland placed on your head.
They are like a beautiful pendant worn around your neck.
passages.original: כִּ֤י׀ לִוְיַ֤ת חֵ֓ן הֵ֬ם לְרֹאשֶׁ֑ךָ וַ֝עֲנָקִ֗ים לְגַרְגְּרֹתֶֽיךָ׃

passages.text: My son, if sinners entice you, do not yield to them.
passages.sermon:
A father speaks to his son.
He warns his son about sinners.
Sinners may try to entice you.
Do not go along with them.
Do not yield to their temptation.
passages.original: בְּנִ֡י אִם־ יְפַתּ֥וּךָ חַ֝טָּאִ֗ים אַל־ תֹּבֵֽא׃

passages.text: If they say, “Come along, let us lie in wait for blood, let us ambush the innocent without cause, let us swallow them alive like Sheol, and whole like those descending into the Pit.
passages.sermon:
Sinners may speak to you.
They may say, "Come with us."
They may invite you to join them.
They may plan to attack someone.
They may want to ambush an innocent person.
They may have no reason to harm this person.
They may say, "Let us swallow them alive."
They may want to destroy the innocent completely.
They may act like Sheol, which takes people alive.
They may want to take the innocent away, whole and unharmed.
They may act like those who go down into the grave.
passages.original: אִם־ יֹאמְרוּ֮ לְכָ֪ה אִ֫תָּ֥נוּ נֶאֶרְבָ֥ה לְדָ֑ם נִצְפְּנָ֖ה לְנָקִ֣י חִנָּֽם׃ נִ֭בְלָעֵם כִּשְׁא֣וֹל חַיִּ֑ים וּ֝תְמִימִ֗ים כְּי֣וֹרְדֵי בֽוֹר׃

passages.text: We will find all manner of precious goods; we will fill our houses with plunder.
passages.sermon:
Sinners speak to you.
They promise you riches.
They say, "We will find valuable things."
They say, "We will fill our houses with stolen goods."
They want to gain wealth through wrongdoing.
passages.original: כָּל־ ה֣וֹן יָקָ֣ר נִמְצָ֑א נְמַלֵּ֖א בָתֵּ֣ינוּ שָׁלָֽל׃

passages.text: Throw in your lot with us; let us all share one purse”— my son, do not walk the road with them or set foot upon their path.
passages.sermon:
Evil people invite others to join them.
They say, "Throw in your lot with us."
They say, "Let us all share one purse."
They want to share stolen goods together.
My son, do not go with them.
Do not walk on their road.
Keep your feet away from their path.
passages.original: גּ֭וֹרָ֣לְךָ תַּפִּ֣יל בְּתוֹכֵ֑נוּ כִּ֥יס אֶ֝חָ֗ד יִהְיֶ֥ה לְכֻלָּֽנוּ׃ בְּנִ֗י אַל־ תֵּלֵ֣ךְ בְּדֶ֣רֶךְ אִתָּ֑ם מְנַ֥ע רַ֝גְלְךָ֗ מִנְּתִיבָתָֽם׃

passages.text: For their feet run to evil, and they are swift to shed blood.
passages.sermon:
These people choose to do evil.
They hurry to commit wrong.
They are quick to harm others.
They are eager to shed blood.
passages.original: כִּ֣י רַ֭גְלֵיהֶם לָרַ֣ע יָר֑וּצוּ וִֽ֝ימַהֲר֗וּ לִשְׁפָּךְ־ דָּֽם׃

passages.text: How futile it is to spread the net where any bird can see it!
passages.sermon:
A person spreads a net.
A bird sees the net.
The net is not hidden.
The bird avoids the net.
Spreading a net in plain sight is useless.
It is foolish to set a trap where everyone can see it.
passages.original: כִּֽי־ חִ֭נָּם מְזֹרָ֣ה הָרָ֑שֶׁת בְּ֝עֵינֵ֗י כָל־ בַּ֥עַל כָּנָֽף׃

passages.text: But they lie in wait for their own blood; they ambush their own lives.
passages.sermon:
These people are evil.
They plan to harm others.
They wait in secret.
They set traps.
But they hurt themselves.
They wait to spill blood.
But it is their own blood.
They ambush others.
But they destroy their own lives.
passages.original: וְ֭הֵם לְדָמָ֣ם יֶאֱרֹ֑בוּ יִ֝צְפְּנ֗וּ לְנַפְשֹׁתָֽם׃

passages.text: Such is the fate of all who are greedy, whose unjust gain takes the lives of its possessors.
passages.sermon:
Greedy people seek unjust gain.
Unjust gain destroys those who possess it.
Greed leads to death for its owner.
This is the fate of everyone who is greedy.
passages.original: כֵּ֗ן אָ֭רְחוֹת כָּל־ בֹּ֣צֵֽעַ בָּ֑צַע אֶת־ נֶ֖פֶשׁ בְּעָלָ֣יו יִקָּֽח׃פ

passages.text: Wisdom calls out in the street, she lifts her voice in the square; in the main concourse she cries aloud, at the city gates she makes her speech: “How long, O simple ones, will you love your simple ways? How long will scoffers delight in their scorn and fools hate knowledge?
passages.sermon:
Wisdom is a woman.
She stands outside.
She calls out in the street.
She raises her voice in the public square.
She cries out at the busiest places.
She speaks at the entrances to the city gates.
She says her words to everyone.
She asks, “How long will you simple people love being simple?
How long will mockers find joy in mocking?
How long will fools hate knowledge?”
passages.original: חָ֭כְמוֹת בַּח֣וּץ תָּרֹ֑נָּה בָּ֝רְחֹב֗וֹת תִּתֵּ֥ן קוֹלָֽהּ׃ בְּרֹ֥אשׁ הֹמִיּ֗וֹת תִּ֫קְרָ֥א בְּפִתְחֵ֖י שְׁעָרִ֥ים בָּעִ֗יר אֲמָרֶ֥יהָ תֹאמֵֽר׃ עַד־ מָתַ֣י׀ פְּתָיִם֮ תְּֽאֵהֲב֫וּ פֶ֥תִי וְלֵצִ֗ים לָ֭צוֹן חָמְד֣וּ לָהֶ֑ם וּ֝כְסִילִ֗ים יִשְׂנְאוּ־ דָֽעַת׃

passages.text: If you had repented at my rebuke, then surely I would have poured out my spirit on you; I would have made my words known to you.
passages.sermon:
Wisdom speaks to people who hear her rebuke.
If you had turned back when I corrected you, I would have acted.
I would have poured out my spirit on you.
I would have made my words known to you.
passages.original: תָּשׁ֗וּבוּ לְֽת֫וֹכַחְתִּ֥י הִנֵּ֤ה אַבִּ֣יעָה לָכֶ֣ם רוּחִ֑י אוֹדִ֖יעָה דְבָרַ֣י אֶתְכֶֽם׃

passages.text: Because you refused my call, and no one took my outstretched hand, because you neglected all my counsel, and wanted none of my correction, in turn I will mock your calamity; I will sneer when terror strikes you, when your dread comes like a storm, and your destruction like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish overwhelm you.
passages.sermon:
Wisdom is speaking.
Wisdom called out to the people.
The people refused to listen.
Wisdom reached out her hand.
No one paid attention.
The people ignored all of Wisdom’s advice.
They did not accept her correction.
Because of this, Wisdom will laugh when disaster comes to them.
Wisdom will mock them when terror strikes.
Terror will come to them suddenly, like a storm.
Disaster will sweep over them like a whirlwind.
Trouble and distress will fall on them.
passages.original: יַ֣עַן קָ֭רָאתִי וַתְּמָאֵ֑נוּ נָטִ֥יתִי יָ֝דִ֗י וְאֵ֣ין מַקְשִֽׁיב׃ וַתִּפְרְע֥וּ כָל־ עֲצָתִ֑י וְ֝תוֹכַחְתִּ֗י לֹ֣א אֲבִיתֶֽם׃ גַּם־ אֲ֭נִי בְּאֵידְכֶ֣ם אֶשְׂחָ֑ק אֶ֝לְעַ֗ג בְּבֹ֣א פַחְדְּכֶֽם׃ בְּבֹ֤א כְשַׁאֲוָה פַּחְדְּכֶ֗ם וְֽ֭אֵידְכֶם כְּסוּפָ֣ה יֶאֱתֶ֑ה בְּבֹ֥א עֲ֝לֵיכֶ֗ם צָרָ֥ה וְצוּקָֽה׃

passages.text: Then they will call on me, but I will not answer; they will earnestly seek me, but will not find me.
passages.sermon:
God speaks to people who have rejected His wisdom and correction.
They will call out to God.
God will not answer them.
They will search for God with great effort.
They will not find Him.
passages.original: אָ֣ז יִ֭קְרָאֻנְנִי וְלֹ֣א אֶֽעֱנֶ֑ה יְ֝שַׁחֲרֻ֗נְנִי וְלֹ֣א יִמְצָאֻֽנְנִי׃

passages.text: For they hated knowledge and chose not to fear the LORD.
passages.sermon: These people hated knowledge.\r\nThey did not choose to fear the LORD.
passages.original: תַּ֭חַת כִּי־ שָׂ֣נְאוּ דָ֑עַת וְיִרְאַ֥ת יְ֝הֹוָ֗ה לֹ֣א בָחָֽרוּ׃

passages.text: They accepted none of my counsel; they despised all my reproof.
passages.sermon:
The people refused my advice.
They did not accept my counsel.
They rejected all my correction.
They despised every warning I gave.
God spoke to them with wisdom and correction.
They chose not to listen to God’s reproof.
passages.original: לֹא־ אָב֥וּ לַעֲצָתִ֑י נָ֝אֲצ֗וּ כָּל־ תּוֹכַחְתִּֽי׃

passages.text: So they will eat the fruit of their own way, and be filled with their own devices.
passages.sermon:
The people hated knowledge.
They chose not to fear the LORD.
They refused my counsel.
They despised all my correction.
They will eat the fruit of their own way.
They will be filled with their own plans.
passages.original: וְֽ֭יֹאכְלוּ מִפְּרִ֣י דַרְכָּ֑ם וּֽמִמֹּעֲצֹ֖תֵיהֶ֣ם יִשְׂבָּֽעוּ׃

passages.text: For the waywardness of the simple will slay them, and the complacency of fools will destroy them.
passages.sermon:
The simple are people who lack wisdom.
The simple turn away from wisdom.
Their waywardness will kill them.
Fools are people who reject understanding.
Fools feel safe and secure in their ignorance.
Their complacency will destroy them.
passages.original: כִּ֤י מְשׁוּבַ֣ת פְּתָיִ֣ם תַּֽהַרְגֵ֑ם וְשַׁלְוַ֖ת כְּסִילִ֣ים תְּאַבְּדֵֽם׃

passages.text: But whoever listens to me will dwell in safety, secure from the fear of evil.”
passages.sermon:
God speaks wisdom.
Whoever listens to God will live in safety.
That person will feel secure.
That person will not fear evil.
passages.original: וְשֹׁמֵ֣עַֽ לִ֭י יִשְׁכָּן־ בֶּ֑טַח וְ֝שַׁאֲנַ֗ן מִפַּ֥חַד רָעָֽה׃פ
